title: Everolimus + exemestane
context_label: Postmenopausal HR-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
schedule_summary: Both tablets are taken every day continuously. There is no planned week off. A four-week blood-test review is a monitoring interval, not a stop-and-restart treatment cycle.
purpose: Exemestane lowers oestrogen production while everolimus blocks an intracellular growth pathway that can contribute to endocrine resistance. The aim in this setting is to control cancer and delay progression.
indication_text: NCCP 00322a: postmenopausal hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without symptomatic visceral disease after recurrence or progression following a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor.
administration_text: Take everolimus at the same time daily, consistently with food or consistently without food. Take exemestane after a meal. Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew. If a dose is missed, take the next scheduled dose without adding an extra dose.
monitoring_summary: Before starting: FBC, renal and liver profile, urea/BUN, urinary protein, blood glucose, cholesterol and triglycerides. Confirm the endocrine indication, review lung symptoms and infections, and check all medicines. Assess bone/fracture risk for the exemestane component. FBC, renal/liver profile, cholesterol and triglycerides every four weeks or as clinically indicated. Check fasting glucose as clinically indicated, with closer monitoring if diabetes or another medicine increases risk. Ask about mouth soreness, infection, cough/breathlessness and daily function at reviews.
review_status: Source-reconciled development content; independent oncology, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Everolimus
agents.explanation: Everolimus binds the intracellular protein FKBP12; this complex inhibits mTORC1, affecting protein synthesis and growth signalling. This pathway can support endocrine resistance, which explains pairing it with an oestrogen-lowering medicine. The same pathway operates in normal tissues, contributing to mouth ulcers, infection risk and metabolic changes.
agents.watch: Report new mouth soreness, cough/breathlessness, fever/infection symptoms, diarrhoea or excessive thirst promptly. A new cough must not simply be labelled drug pneumonitis without checking other causes.
risks: Impaired wound healing and radiation-related toxicity

agents.name: Exemestane
agents.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits aromatase and lowers oestrogen production
agents.explanation: After menopause, aromatase in tissues converts androgen precursors into oestrogen. Exemestane is an irreversible aromatase inhibitor that reduces this supply to hormone-sensitive cancer cells. It does not directly switch off functioning ovaries; the menopausal indication must be confirmed.
agents.watch: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning can be silent, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.

monitoring_schedule.note: Reference timing, not booked appointments. Ask who requests each test, when it is due, who reviews the result and whom to contact if it is missing. Delays can change cycle numbers; time-based monitoring remains time-based.

urgent_extra: Contact the oncology team promptly for new or worsening cough or breathlessness, fever or infection symptoms, mouth sores that prevent drinking/eating, severe diarrhoea or dehydration, or marked thirst and frequent urination. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or swelling of the tongue/throat needs emergency help.

sections.title: Two daily tablets, two different jobs
sections.text: Keep a simple routine for the oral medicines and request your next supply before tablets run out. No port or pump is needed for this regimen itself.

sections.title: Four-week review, continuous treatment
sections.text: A blood-test or pharmacy review every four weeks does not mean a rest week. Follow the prescribed daily doses unless the team explicitly tells you to pause.

sections.title: The first eight weeks: mouth care
sections.text: Agree a mouth-care plan before the first dose. The team may prescribe an alcohol-free steroid mouthwash. Report soreness early, before it affects eating or drinking; use the specific prescribed directions.

sections.title: When one medicine is held
sections.text: Ask the team to state clearly which tablet to pause, whether exemestane should continue, what needs to recover and who will authorise restarting everolimus.

sections.title: Radiotherapy or surgery
sections.text: Tell both teams that you take everolimus. Treatment given during or soon after radiotherapy may increase toxicity, and previous irradiated areas can develop recall inflammation. The teams decide spacing or interruption; there is no universal interval on this card.

sections.title: Response scans
sections.text: Ask which scan will assess benefit and when it is due. Routine response imaging follows your individual plan. New breathing symptoms need earlier assessment rather than waiting for that scan.

evidence.title: BOLERO-2 final progression-free survival analysis
evidence.population: 724 postmenopausal patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after non-steroidal aromatase inhibitors; everolimus+exemestane versus placebo+exemestane.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed PFS: median 7.8 versus 3.2 months; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.38–0.54), p<0.0001. Central review: 11.0 versus 4.1 months.
evidence.interpretation: Investigator-assessed PFS: median 7.8 versus 3.2 months; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.38–0.54), p<0.0001. Central review: 11.0 versus 4.1 months. Adding mTOR inhibition delayed progression compared with exemestane alone in this trial population.
evidence.limitations: Conducted before routine CDK4/6-inhibitor use; the observed benefit is not a guaranteed individual outcome and is not direct randomised evidence for current post-CDK4/6 sequencing.

teachback: Which medicine is taken or given when, what checks are expected next, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: If everolimus is interrupted or reduced for toxicity, NCCP says exemestane may continue; the treating team must confirm the plan for each medicine. Do not stop both automatically or restart everolimus yourself. Everolimus can increase toxicity around radiotherapy and impair wound healing: agree a specific plan before radiotherapy or surgery. This NCCP indication is postmenopausal. If pregnancy remains possible or menopause is uncertain, ask the team to confirm endocrine status and suitable contraception. Everolimus product information advises highly effective contraception during treatment and for eight weeks after it ends; pregnancy and breastfeeding are NCCP exclusions.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: NCCP classifies everolimus as minimal-to-low emetic risk. There are no routine infusion premedications. Any as-needed antiemetic follows the individual prescription and local oral-SACT policy.

support.title: Prevent and treat mouth soreness
support.text: Discuss non-alcoholic mouth care and a prescribed alcohol-free corticosteroid mouthwash during the first eight weeks. Avoid irritating products containing alcohol, hydrogen peroxide, iodine or thyme derivatives. Check for oral thrush; do not automatically add an antifungal.

support.title: Steroids and infection prevention
support.text: Systemic steroids may be needed for pneumonitis. When steroids or other immunosuppressive medicines are used, the team considers PJP prevention; it is not an automatic prescription for every patient.

support.title: Glucose, lipids and bone health
support.text: Manage diabetes and lipid abnormalities alongside treatment. Bone-health advice and medicines depend on fracture risk, DXA findings, diet and vitamin-D status.

support.title: Medicine and supplement review
support.text: Check prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with oncology pharmacy. Avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort; some antibiotics and antifungals can markedly change everolimus exposure.

endocrine_timeline.title: Daily treatment and review milestones
endocrine_timeline.intro: No dates or personal details are needed. Treatment is continuous unless the prescriber changes it; there is no invented chemotherapy rest week.

rows.label: Daily treatment
rows.text: Usual starting doses: everolimus 10 mg once daily and exemestane 25 mg once daily; the prescribed everolimus dose may be lower.

rows.label: Safety monitoring
rows.text: Keep the blood-test and symptom-review plan

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: Exemestane lowers oestrogen production while everolimus blocks an intracellular growth pathway that can contribute to endocrine resistance. The aim in this setting is to control cancer and delay progression.

items.title: Who this covers
items.text: NCCP 00322a: postmenopausal hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without symptomatic visceral disease after recurrence or progression following a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: Usual starting doses: everolimus 10 mg once daily and exemestane 25 mg once daily; the prescribed everolimus dose may be lower.. Take everolimus at the same time daily, consistently with food or consistently without food. Take exemestane after a meal. Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew. items.title: Duration and decisions
items.text: Continue while the treatment is helping and side effects remain manageable, according to the consultant plan. This advanced-disease regimen has no fixed adjuvant completion date.

items.title: Individual safety and source differences
items.text: If everolimus is interrupted or reduced for toxicity, NCCP says exemestane may continue; the treating team must confirm the plan for each medicine. Do not stop both automatically or restart everolimus yourself. Everolimus can increase toxicity around radiotherapy and impair wound healing: agree a specific plan before radiotherapy or surgery.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Blood tests assess treatment safety. Scans assess disease or investigate symptoms. Echo and ECG answer different questions.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Before starting: FBC, renal and liver profile, urea/BUN, urinary protein, blood glucose, cholesterol and triglycerides. Confirm the endocrine indication, review lung symptoms and infections, and check all medicines. Assess bone/fracture risk for the exemestane component.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: FBC, renal/liver profile, cholesterol and triglycerides every four weeks or as clinically indicated. Check fasting glucose as clinically indicated, with closer monitoring if diabetes or another medicine increases risk. Ask about mouth soreness, infection, cough/breathlessness and daily function at reviews.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: NCCP 00322 does not mandate routine ECG or echocardiography. Cardiac tests should follow symptoms, comorbidities and other treatments, rather than a copied HER2-treatment schedule.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Exemestane can reduce bone mineral density. Review fracture risk and arrange DXA and bone protection when indicated. This regimen does not specify a single repeat-DXA interval for everyone.

chapters.title: Your wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Additional treatments depend on the confirmed setting and indication.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. Less frequent monitoring may suit indolent disease. New symptoms or suspected progression need earlier assessment. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not an automatic three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: If informative, particularly when elevated at baseline or disease is not readily measurable, tumour markers may supplement clinical assessment and imaging. A marker rise alone should not trigger a treatment change. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and contraception
items.text: This NCCP indication is postmenopausal. If pregnancy remains possible or menopause is uncertain, ask the team to confirm endocrine status and suitable contraception. Everolimus product information advises highly effective contraception during treatment and for eight weeks after it ends; pregnancy and breastfeeding are NCCP exclusions.

chapters.title: Evidence depends on the population
chapters.intro: Different studies answer different questions; do not compare their results as if populations and follow-up were identical.

items.title: BOLERO-2 overall survival analysis
items.text: Same randomised BOLERO-2 population; overall survival was a key secondary endpoint. Overall survival: median 31.0 versus 26.6 months; HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.73–1.10), p=0.14. No statistically significant overall-survival advantage was demonstrated. Do not present the PFS benefit as proven longer survival. Subsequent therapies were common; OS was secondary, and the confidence interval includes no difference.

items.title: SWISH stomatitis-prevention study
items.text: Single-arm prevention study in 92 postmenopausal women starting everolimus+exemestane; 85 evaluable for the week 8 stomatitis endpoint in the EU SmPC report. EU SmPC reports Grade ≥2 stomatitis at 8 weeks in 2/85 (2.4%); no Grade 3/4 cases. Supports discussing a prescribed alcohol-free dexamethasone mouthwash early in treatment. Study regimen: 0.5 mg/5 mL solution, 10 mL swished for 2 minutes and spat four times daily for 8 weeks; local formulation/prescribing review is needed. Single-arm study with historical comparison, not a randomised concurrent control; oral candidiasis occurred and the mouthwash is a separate prescription.
